title: On the product of cross-intersecting families with small covering number
summary: A central problem in extremal set theory is to determine or estimate $m(n,k,t),n>2k\geq 2t$, the maximum size of an intersecting $k$-graph and covering number at least $t$(see the paper for the definitions). For $t=1$ and $2$ the classical Erdős-Ko-Rado Theorem and the Hilton-Milner Theorem provide the answer.The complete solution for $t=3$ was only achieved recently . There are some partial results for $t=4,5$ but for the general case even to determine the asymptotic appears to be hopelessly difficult .
